summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease with two kidney transplants, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, peripheral arterial disease with left below-knee amputation, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for hypertensive urgency with systolic blood pressures reaching 244 mmHg, associated with chest tightness and mild pulmonary edema. The episode was partly attributed to unintentional underdosing of labetalol due to a change in tablet strength. He also experienced transient epigastric pain concerning for mesenteric ischemia, though workup was negative. His blood pressure was stabilized with IV nitroglycerin initially, followed by transition to oral amlodipine, doxazosin, hydralazine, and increased labetalol, while nifedipine was discontinued. He received IV furosemide for pulmonary congestion and was transitioned back to home torsemide. His platelet count, which dipped during admission, normalized. He was discharged home on an adjusted antihypertensive regimen with close follow-up for transplant care, sleep apnea reassessment, and monitoring of kidney mass and medication levels.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease
Peripheral artery disease with left below knee amputation
